newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank H1 oper profit up 15.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank H1 oper profit up 15.2 pct.

text.p: Six months to June 30
(in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Group oper profit after provisions 765.7 up 15.2 pct
Group own-account trading income 197.2 vs 191.8
Group net interest income 2,500 up 7.9 pct
Group net commission income 697.8 up 19.9 pct
Group risk provisions 498.5 up 13.1 pct
Group administration costs 2,100 up 7.8 pct
NOTE - Full name of the German bank is Bayerische Vereinsbank AG. The bank on Monday announced it plans to merge with fellow Bavarian bank Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG.
Analysts on average predicted an operating profit of 815 million marks on average, up 22.6 percent.

The bank said it expected to post a good result for the coming year. "It thus sees itself excellently prepared for the new dynamic from the planned fusion with Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank," it said in a statement.

Vereinsbank said its banking business contributed 277 million marks to its operating profit while mortgage banking business contributed 488.7 million marks. Some 77 percent of the operating profit was achieved at home.

Interest income was the biggest contributor to earnings, where the biggest rise was in income from mortgage lending, which rose 12.2 percent to 800 million marks. The volume of new lending for private homes rose 11 percent to 9.8 billion marks.
Interest income from banking business rose six percent to 1.7 billion marks.
In trading income, Vereinsbank itself contributed 68 percent of the result while its subsidiary Vereins und West-Bank contributed 25 percent.
Personnel costs rose 5.9 percent while other spending rose 10.8 percent, reflecting efforts to improve company management and risk controls to create a basis for higher profitability.
Risk provisions on lending business fell slightly despite higher insolvencies, the bank said, reaching 561.9 million marks versus 579.4 million in the year-ago period.
Group assets under management 67,500 up 16.2 pct
Staff (versus 31 Dec 1996) 21,482 vs 21,825
